architecture.mechanism: Acoustic beamforming with a diagonal double rectangular microphone array combined with MVDR and LSTM processing enables non-contact, high-accuracy fault identification for belt conveyor idlers over long distances in noisy environments.
architecture.intervention: Install a small number of fixed diagonal double rectangular microphone arrays at strategic positions along the conveyor gallery in the dusty/humid plant areas to passively capture acoustic emissions from the 4000 rollers; run MVDR+LSTM inference on edge hardware to estimate fault (bearing wear) location and stage without placing any sensor on individual rollers, achieving retrofit cost under $15 per roller and zero production downtime.
architecture.expected_effect: Early bearing wear across the 4000-roller fleet is detected indirectly via acoustic monitoring with localization sufficient to identify the worn roller for replacement, with a false-alarm rate held under 2% per month through the noise-robustness of MVDR and the time-series discrimination of LSTM.
architecture.falsification_test: Deploy the array system on a representative section of conveyor (≥200 rollers) for 3 months under the plant's actual dust and humidity; measure false-alarm rate per month and verify it remains <2%, confirm that bearings flagged by the system show measurable wear upon inspection, and confirm that unflagged bearings run without failure during the test window.
